answer: Each identity locks its own 60-credit bond on a mesa board. Any peer may claim two identities share one operator; ocean reviewers check their samples, and each challenged identity must answer with its own lantern key. A proven claim pays 24, burns 36, and strips both fakes. Sealing is superlinear: the kth fake's handler could earn 24k, so that fake costs 60 plus 24k; 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 in bonds plus 12,012,000 in bribes. A bribe is a record another handler can claim on; a false claim forfeits the claimant's bond. An honest agent locks 60 once, back after three clean epochs.
